name: reading-quiz
what: A reader holding only the skill, its references and its four agents answers what the text requires at its densest points. Each wrong option differs from the right one in one detail; the options are shuffled per question by its id.

questions.q: Where does the review's file set come from?
options: The tasks' implementation and proof records, plus any path the person says the change reached; never discovered
The tasks' implementation and proof records, plus any path `git diff` shows under the target source root
The tasks' implementation records alone; proof records name tests, which the coverage pass finds itself
The paths the trace binds to the tasks' nodes, read from siegard-trace.json

questions.q: A path an implementation record names that the target source root no longer holds (a file the delivery deleted). What does the review do with it?
options: Leaves it out of the file set and names it in the report as not read
Keeps it in the file set and records a finding that it cannot be read
Stops the review, since a path the root cannot read stops its pass
Leaves it out of the file set silently, since it was never in the set

questions.q: The invocation names no review name. What is the review called, and what if that name is taken?
options: The initiative's slug; a name already taken under run/, review/ or siegard-reconcile/ is a stop
The initiative's slug; a taken name gets a numeric suffix so the earlier record stays
The task's identifier; a name already taken under run/, review/ or siegard-reconcile/ is a stop
The initiative's slug; a taken name is a stop only where run.py refuses it

questions.q: Where does the project's standard come from when the invocation names one and siegard.json declares a different one for the target?
options: The invocation's naming wins, and the report gives both
siegard.json wins, as it does for the roots, and the report gives both
The invocation's naming wins, and the report gives only the one used
Neither: two differing standards join the single stop of absent inputs

questions.q: siegard.json declares `null` as the standard for this target. What happens?
options: The standard pass does not run, and the record says the project authored none for this target
The standard joins the single stop of absent inputs, with the /siegard-config invocation ready
The standard pass does not run, and the record says the input was not given
Another target's standard line is used, since the project declares one

questions.q: Does a review carry a pin of the tasks it answers?
options: No; it answers the criteria its tasks state today, and an earlier review over a task changed since is never refused for it
Yes; it pins each task's digest, and `--review` refuses a review whose task changed since
No; it answers the criteria its tasks state today, and an earlier review over a task changed since is refused by deliver.py --check
Yes, but only for the standard, whose pin `--review` compares against the task's

questions.q: Under `trace.py --stage --review`, which node-file pair is left out of the judges' packs?
options: One a reconciliation's judgment cleared at the very bytes on disk (`judged`), its node unchanged since and no finding standing against it
One a delivery's bind stamped at the very bytes on disk, its node unchanged since and no finding standing against it
One a reconciliation's judgment cleared at the very bytes on disk, even where it is a node the tasks implement
Any pair whose trace binding shows no drift

questions.q: A file of the set that the trace binds nothing to (a test, say). What does the staging do with it?
options: Hands it a judge over the plan's nodes alone, and stages it under `unbound`
Hands it no judge, and stages it under `unbound`
Hands it a judge over the plan's nodes alone, and binds them to it at the fold
Hands it a judge over every node of the candidate index

questions.q: How are the conformance judges dispatched?
options: One per file the manifest holds, by the waves the staging receipt lists; the next wave only once `--save-return` reports 0 pending
One per file the manifest holds, by the waves the staging receipt lists; the next wave once the session has counted every notification of the last
One per node the manifest holds, by the waves the staging receipt lists; the next wave only once `--save-return` reports 0 pending
One judge over the whole file set, so no pair is judged twice

questions.q: The harness refuses a launch within a wave. What is the route?
options: The wave was cut too wide: report `--stage --concurrency <fewer>` ready to run again
Dispatch the refused judge again on its own, after the rest of the wave returns
Run the refused file's judgment inline and say so in the report
Re-stage with `--concurrency <fewer>` yourself and continue without reporting it

questions.q: A saved conformance return is one the fold will refuse. What do you do?
options: Run a fresh subagent with the prompt fixed, before the wave closes
Repair the saved YAML so it holds to conformance-return.json, saying so in the report
Send a follow-up message to the same subagent asking it to fix its reply
Fold anyway; the fold drops the unusable return and the record notes it

questions.q: What does `trace.py --bind-record` write after the fold?
options: Exactly the pairs the judgment cleared — the delivery's own nodes and every other node's claim on these files — never with `--replace`
Exactly the pairs the judgment cleared, with `--replace`, so releases owed are applied at once
Every pair the staging read, cleared or not, so the trace shows what was judged
Only the delivery's own nodes; other nodes' claims on these files wait for /reconcile

questions.q: When does the failures pass run?
options: Where a run was captured and it did not pass — including a run whose outcome says nothing executed
Where a run was captured, whatever its outcome, so a green run is also diagnosed
Where a run was captured and a step failed; a run whose outcome says nothing executed is an absent input
Only where the person named a run already captured

questions.q: How do the certification pass and the coverage pass differ?
options: Coverage asks whether the tests prove the task's criteria; certification asks whether one test proves one node's fact — and only its `covered`, with the conformance pass clearing the node as well, makes the binding one a test decides
Coverage asks whether the tests prove the task's criteria; certification asks whether one test proves one node's fact — and its `covered` alone makes the binding one a test decides
Certification replaces coverage for any node a proof's test demonstrates
Coverage asks whether the tests prove one node's fact; certification asks whether they prove the task's criteria

questions.q: Where does a certification claim come from?
options: The `demonstrates` entries of the proof records passed under `--demonstrated`, or a `--certify` file a person states — never both for one node
The `demonstrates` entries of the proof records passed under `--demonstrated`, or the session's own reading of which test proves which node
Any node whose kind is `policy`, since a policy names one input against one result
The `demonstrates` entries, or a `--certify` file; a node under both takes the `--certify` one

questions.q: What does the report do with the findings?
options: Opens with counts from `deliver.py --findings`, grouped by pass, kind, rule, cause and file, each group beside the route a repair would take; it never ranks a group or decides a route
Opens with counts from `deliver.py --findings`, grouped by pass, kind, rule, cause and file, and recommends which group to repair first
Opens with each finding in full, then the counts, each group beside the route a repair would take
Opens with counts the session tallies from the review record, grouped by pass and file

questions.q: Which invocation does the review's handoff hand forward?
options: None: the skeleton marks no door, and a finding's route handed as a decision is the person's own
The `/implement-task` invocation over the task, for each finding against source
The `/analyse` invocation, for each unstated fact the conformance pass found
None, except a `/reconcile` invocation where the trace shows drift

questions.q: Besides the delivery root, what may the review write?
options: The reconciliation record and its returns under siegard-reconcile/ and siegard-trace.json, at the target's git toplevel
The reconciliation record and its returns under siegard-reconcile/, siegard-trace.json, and delivery.json written by hand
The reconciliation record under siegard-reconcile/ alone; the bind is /reconcile's
siegard-trace.json and the task files whose criteria the coverage pass found unmet
